summary: Build a Docker-based job recommendation portal with a Next.js frontend, FastAPI API, and scheduled Python agent worker. Users manage a resume and job preferences, review explained recommendations, and open external application pages themselves; discovery must use authorized sources and must not collect or inject LinkedIn session state.

workspaceSignals.decisionReason: The workspace has no application manifests or existing service implementation; the existing files are a blueprint and test note only.

questions.question: Which programming language for Job Recommendation Portal?
questions.rationale: The existing blueprint specifies Next.js with TypeScript.

questions.question: Which frontend framework for Job Recommendation Portal?
questions.rationale: The existing blueprint specifies Next.js App Router; containerization will be part of the project setup.

options.label: Next.js
options.description: React framework with App Router and server rendering

questions.question: Describe the features for Job Recommendation Portal.
questions.answer: Provide onboarding for target job titles, skills, and resume PDF; a recommendation review queue with match explanations and approve/skip controls; an application action that opens the external job application page without submitting; and a History tab showing scheduled run status and results.
questions.rationale: Distilled from the user's requested portal behavior.

questions.question: Describe the features or API routes for Jobs API.
questions.answer: Support authenticated user profiles, target titles and skills, PDF resume metadata and secure file access, recommendation explanations, approve/skip decisions, external application links, and read-only discovery-run history. Do not store LinkedIn passwords or session cookies. Only support application submission through a separately authorized integration, if explicitly configured.

questions.rationale: The existing blueprint specifies Python for the agent engine; the user requests a scheduled worker.

questions.question: Which framework for Scheduled Discovery and Agent Worker?
questions.rationale: A single Docker-based worker with a twice-daily schedule is explicitly requested; a dedicated queue is not.

options.label: Python worker with APScheduler
options.description: Run scheduled discovery twice daily in a container

options.label: Python worker with Celery Beat
options.description: Scheduled tasks with a distributed task queue

questions.question: Describe the features for Scheduled Discovery and Agent Worker.
questions.answer: Run job discovery twice daily using authorized public job sources, documented APIs, or public ATS feeds. Rank and explain recommendations against the user's skills and resume, record run status/results for History, and never scrape LinkedIn or inject browser/session state. Applying remains user-controlled through an external application link.

Rank and explain recommendations against the user's skills and resume, record run status/results for History, and never scrape LinkedIn or inject browser/session state. Applying remains user-controlled through an external application link.
